objectives.wording: Distinguish growth from development and explain major determinants of normal growth.
Measure and plot age-appropriate parameters using relevant WHO or Indian standards and interpret serial trends.
Identify abnormal trajectories on supplied growth charts and justify referral.
Map motor, behavioural, social, adaptive and language milestones and select appropriate assessment methods.
Use a simulated history and growth trajectory to prioritize causes, assessment and care.
Discuss growth concerns, a feasible feeding plan and follow-up with a simulated caregiver.
Interpret height, growth velocity and family context and justify evaluation and management.
Define developmental delay and classify causes of delay and disability, including intellectual disability.
Demonstrate a structured approach to a simulated child with developmental delay.
Explain findings and uncertainty and agree on referral and early support in simulation.
Observe a visit and document the team's roles and assessment and follow-up workflow.
Explain contributing factors and distinguish ADHD from mimics using symptoms, impairment and reports across settings.
Explain contributing factors, recognize developmental features and outline diagnostic assessment and individualized support.
Describe the clinical features, diagnosis and management of feeding problems in children.
Describe the clinical features, diagnosis and management of breath-holding spells and distinguish them from mimics.
Describe the clinical features, diagnosis and management of temper tantrums, distinguishing developmental behaviour from concerns requiring evaluation.
Describe the clinical features, diagnosis and management of pica.
Classify enuresis and relate its aetiology and clinical features to management.
Define adolescence and compare the characteristics of its stages.
Identify common physical and psychosocial concerns and explain preventive assessment.
Demonstrate a private consultation and explain confidentiality and its limits.
Demonstrate a simulated check with focused history, growth charts, sexual maturity rating, thyroid and breast assessment where appropriate, and HEADSS screening.
Observe a clinic and describe its access, counselling and referral workflow.
Explain the objectives and functions of Adolescent Friendly Health Services and match representative presentations to referral criteria.
Compare physical, physiological and psychological changes across puberty.
Compare anorexia nervosa and bulimia by presentation and identify complications and referral needs.
Recognize common presentations and identify situations requiring further assessment.
Explain the importance of recognising risk factors for obesity and other noncommunicable diseases in adolescents and outline prevention opportunities.
Compare contributing factors, clinical findings and management principles.
Assess representative risk factors and identify prevention measures at family and community levels.
Elicit diet and activity history, perform dietary recall and plot growth in simulation.
In a skills station, examine a child with obesity, calculating BMI, measuring waist-to-hip ratio and identifying acanthosis, striae and pseudogynaecomastia.
